target.title: fix(parallel): resolve env search key refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Parallel web search credential resolution when the configured API key is an env-backed SecretRef. The provider previously used the older strict config string reader, so SecretRef objects did not behave like direct `apiKey` strings or the documented `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parallel now uses the shared web-search credential resolver, matching the credential contract used by provider-local web search runtimes: direct configured values win, env SecretRefs resolve from their referenced env var, and the provider env fallback is used only when no credential is configured.

## User Impact

Users can configure `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey` as an env SecretRef without needing a live key in config. Missing or unsupported SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently falling back to an unrelated ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` value.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 35 tests.

## Proof

- Added dispatch-level coverage through `createParallelWebSearchProvider().createTool(...).execute(...)`, lazy runtime loading, plugin-owned `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey`, scoped config merge, and the mocked trusted endpoint request.
- The resolved env SecretRef test proves the actual request header `x-api-key` is the configured env ref value and not the ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.
- The unavailable env SecretRef test sets ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, configures a missing env SecretRef, expects `missing_parallel_api_key`, and proves zero endpoint calls were made.
- Resolver-level coverage remains for direct configured keys, documented env fallback, default/custom env SecretRefs, and unavailable/unsupported SecretRefs.

target.title: fix(tasks): deliver corrected terminal outcomes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an older terminal notification could finish sending after a task had acquired a newer terminal outcome and then mark that newer outcome as already delivered. Users could receive the stale success/cancellation message while the corrected failure or summary was permanently suppressed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Terminal delivery now uses one canonical projection containing the owner, route, rendered payload, delivery capability, and an idempotency key fingerprinted from the actual destination and content. The registry revalidates that projection before sending, after a successful send, and before fallback. If a newer generation replaces an in-flight notification, the old completion cannot mutate the new delivery state and the newer notifier is scheduled immediately.

## User Impact

When a task's terminal status, error, summary, or destination changes during delivery, users receive the corrected terminal notification. Repeating an identical terminal projection remains idempotent and does not resend.

## Evidence

AI-assisted change. I reviewed the state-machine transitions and test scenarios.

Focused regressions cover:

- an old send resolving after `succeeded` / `blocked` becomes `failed`;
- an old send rejecting after the terminal generation changes;
- same status/outcome with changed error or summary while the first send is pending;
- a correction after the old payload was already delivered;
- an identical terminal repeat remaining single-delivery.

target.title: fix(agents): honor aborts during context preflight
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent run could remain stuck in Context Engine bootstrap, maintenance, session-lock acquisition, or assembly after the caller cancelled the run or its attempt deadline expired. In the embedded runner this could also consume the whole run budget before the active watchdog was armed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The embedded attempt now establishes one deadline before Context Engine preflight and carries the remaining budget into the active-run watchdog. The same run abort signal is passed through the public Context Engine bootstrap, maintenance, and assembly contracts, including the CLI and Codex harnesses. Abort is terminal instead of falling through to baseline context, and session-mutating bootstrap keeps the write lock until the engine has actually settled.

Assembly can be abandoned promptly by the host. Bootstrap and maintenance are deliberately cooperative: an engine must observe the new optional `abortSignal`, while OpenClaw keeps the write lock until an uncooperative operation really settles so late writes cannot escape lock ownership.

## User Impact

Cancelled or timed-out runs no longer continue into a model call after Context Engine preflight. Cooperative engines stop bootstrap and maintenance at the run boundary, pending assembly stops blocking the attempt, and the active model phase cannot receive a fresh timeout budget after slow preflight.

## Evidence

AI-assisted change. I reviewed the implementation, its lock/cancellation invariants, and the generated tests.

- Deterministic embedded-run regressions hold bootstrap, assembly, and initial session-lock acquisition pending, then trigger caller abort or the run deadline. They prove the attempt settles and that the write lock is not released before cooperative bootstrap settlement.
- CLI and Codex regressions hold Context Engine bootstrap pending, abort the run, and prove the CLI backend / Codex `thread/start` is never started.
- Direct dependency inspection: current sibling Codex handles model work only after `thread/start`; `turn/interrupt` targets startup or an existing turn. Context Engine projection happens before that protocol boundary, so OpenClaw must own preflight cancellation.

The character that fronts the entire first-run experience never reacts to it, and there is nothing playful to discover. ## Why This Change Was Made The shared mascot view now has a small behavior engine (`OpenClawMascotAnimator`) that owns per-mood animation loops, entrance gestures, randomized micro-behavior, and interaction Easter eggs, while the drawing stays in the existing `Canvas` vector (new pose channels: gaze, eyelids, happy-arc eyes, mouth, blush, body tilt/squash, antenna droop, dizzy eyes, sparkle/heart/zzz particles). target.title: fix(agents): honor Anthropic Retry-After in auto-retry backoff (#103849)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On the default Anthropic Messages transport (used by every `anthropic-messages` model), a 429 response carrying a server-specified `Retry-After` header is turned into a plain `Error` with no status or retry-after data attached. `AgentSession.prepareRetry` therefore always falls back to fixed exponential backoff (2s / 4s / 8s) regardless of the server's cooldown. With `maxRetries: 3`, all three retries can land inside a still-active 30-second rate-limit window and the turn fails outright instead of succeeding after the server's actual cooldown.

Closes #103849

## Why This Change Was Made

The bespoke fetch client behind the managed transport is not a Stainless-style SDK, so the `Retry-After` value parsed upstream is only used to set an `x-should-retry` header this client never reads. The header is discarded before the error reaches `prepareRetry`, whose delay formula has no input for a server-prescribed wait.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`** — non-OK responses throw via `createAnthropicMessagesHttpError`, attaching `status`/`httpStatus` and a `retryAfterSeconds` parsed with the **canonical** `parseRetryAfterSeconds` (now exported from `provider-transport-fetch.ts` — no divergent duplicate).
- **`src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`** — `extractTransportErrorDetails` propagates `httpStatus`/`retryAfterSeconds` from the thrown error onto the AssistantMessage.
- **`packages/llm-core/src/types.ts`** — `AssistantMessage` gains optional `httpStatus?` / `retryAfterSeconds?` (additive; no migration required).
- **`src/llm/utils/retry.ts`** — `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs` uses the server cooldown as a lower bound for the exponential delay, bounded by the operator-configured `retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs` (default 60s). It lives here (not in the session module) so it is not re-exported through the plugin-sdk barrel, keeping the public SDK surface unchanged.
- **`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`** — `prepareRetry` passes `getProviderRetrySettings().maxRetryDelayMs` and handles the reject case.

### Retry-After bound (respects existing config; no arbitrary ceiling)

The ceiling is the existing operator setting `retry.provider.maxRetryDelayMs` (default 60s, "max server-requested delay before failing"), not a magic number:

- A cooldown **within** the configured max is honored **in full** — including values above 60s when the operator raises the limit (never silently shortened into the active window).
- A cooldown that **exceeds** the configured max returns `null`, so `prepareRetry` **stops retrying in-turn** and lets provider fallback / operator recovery proceed — instead of holding the session asleep for minutes or hours. This resolves the `merge-risk: availability` and `merge-risk: compatibility` concerns.
- An overflowed/malformed numeric header (canonical parser yields `Infinity`) is rejected, not silently collapsed to the short exponential schedule.

## User Impact

Anthropic 429s with a `Retry-After` within the configured tolerance now delay the automatic retry by at least the server window (so rate-limited turns wait out the cooldown and succeed); cooldowns beyond the tolerance fail fast for fallback rather than stalling the session.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof (end to end, accepted + rejected).** A real Node HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` responds with HTTP 429 + a `Retry-After` header, driven through the real `createAnthropicMessagesTransportStreamFn()` (real `buildGuardedModelFetch`); the stub endpoint is the only mock. The propagated `retryAfterSeconds` is fed into the real `resolveAutoRetryDelayMs` with the default `maxRetryDelayMs=60000`:

```
configured maxRetryDelayMs=60000
ACCEPTED (retry-after: 30):  httpStatus=429 retryAfterSeconds=30  -> prepareRetry delay=30000ms
REJECTED (retry-after: 120): httpStatus=429 retryAfterSeconds=120 -> prepareRetry delay=null (stop retrying -> fallback)
```

Before this fix (origin/main) the same 429 yields `httpStatus=null`, `retryAfterSeconds=null`, and a fixed 2000ms backoff.

**Focused tests.**
- `src/llm/utils/retry.auto-retry-delay.test.ts` — exponential fallback, lower-bound, boundary at max, reject above max, reject `Infinity`, honor >60s when the operator raises the max, invalid-hint fallback.
- `src/agents/provider-transport-fetch.test.ts` — canonical `parseRetryAfterSeconds` across all forms + overflow header → `Infinity`.
- `src/agents/transport-stream-shared.test.ts` — status/retry-after propagation onto the AssistantMessage.

target.title: fix(extensions/anthropic): preserve migrated model entries when inherited keys shadow converted refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where adopting Claude CLI auth could silently drop a model's custom settings (aliases, parameters, etc.) or throw when the global `Object.prototype` contains an inherited property matching the converted Anthropic model ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteModelEntryMap` used `converted in next` to decide whether to copy a legacy `claude-cli/*` entry to its Anthropic equivalent, and then assigned with `next[converted] = value`. The `in` operator follows the prototype chain, and the assignment can throw or invoke an inherited setter when `Object.prototype` is polluted. The migration could therefore skip the copy, delete the original `claude-cli/*` key, and lose the user's model configuration.

The change now:
- checks own-property membership with `Object.hasOwn`;
- writes migrated and seeded entries with `Object.defineProperty` so they become own properties even when `Object.prototype` has a getter-only accessor, non-writable data descriptor, or setter.

This applies the same own-entry invariant that #103373 adds to the Anthropic API-key default-allowlist seeding path.

## User Impact

Users whose runtime has a polluted `Object.prototype` no longer lose per-model aliases or other metadata, and no longer see migration throws, when adopting Claude CLI-backed Anthropic refs.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```bash
pnpm test extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts --run
```

Result: 19 passed.

The regression suite covers four Object.prototype descriptor collisions and fails against the parent commit:
- inherited writable data descriptor;
- inherited non-writable data descriptor (throws before the fix);
- inherited getter-only accessor (throws before the fix);
- inherited setter accessor (entry becomes undefined before the fix, setter is not invoked after).

### Type / lint

```bash
pnpm tsgo:extensions        # exit 0
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.ts
```

Both pass.

### Live migration proof

Controlled run with an `Object.prototype` getter-only accessor shadowing the converted ref:

```text
=== Claude CLI auth adoption migration proof ===
Scenario: Object.prototype has a getter-only accessor for the converted ref.
Migrated entry: {
  "alias": "Work Opus",
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" }
}
Entry is own property: true
Alias preserved: true
Parameters preserved: true
```

The alias and `temperature` parameter survive migration, and the resulting entry is an own property of `models` rather than the inherited accessor value.

## Release Note

- Anthropic: preserve migrated model aliases and parameters when inherited prototype keys shadow converted Claude CLI refs.

Related: #103373

target.title: feat(discord): show subagent progress
target.body:
## Summary

Adds opt-in Discord-scoped sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message, including count reactions, durable failure marker behavior, and typing keepalive while tracked work is active.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord users currently have little visible feedback when an assistant turn delegates work to tracked sub-agents. Long-running turns can look idle after the initial message even though background sub-agents are still running, and a sub-agent failure is not visible on the original Discord message.

Discord also cannot represent concurrent work by adding the same emoji reaction multiple times from the same bot/user, so progress needs a count-based reaction model instead of repeated identical reactions.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

Discord users get immediate, lightweight progress feedback during delegated work without waiting for the final assistant reply:

- `1️⃣`, `2️⃣`, etc. show the current active tracked sub-agent count for the turn
- the count reaction is replaced as the active count changes
- the count reaction disappears when no tracked sub-agents remain active
- `🔴` remains if any tracked sub-agent ends with a non-OK outcome
- typing stays active while tracked sub-agents are still running

Operators can configure the behavior with `channels.discord.subagentProgress`, including reaction progress, count emoji, failure emoji, typing keepalive, interval, and max-duration TTL.

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

## Linked Context

No linked issues or external context were listed in the current PR body.

## What Changes

This PR adds Discord-scoped, best-effort sub-agent progress feedback on the original inbound Discord message. The feature is opt-in with `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`.

When enabled:

- one configurable count reaction shows the number of currently active tracked sub-agents (`1️⃣` … `🔟` by default)
- count changes replace the previous count reaction instead of accumulating multiple ordinal reactions
- zero active tracked sub-agents removes the count reaction
- any non-OK completion leaves a durable configurable failure marker (`🔴` by default)
- Discord typing is kept alive independently while tracked sub-agents remain active, then stops when all tracked work finishes or the safety TTL expires

The implementation threads the source Discord message id through native `sessions_spawn`, tracked ACP spawn, requester origin metadata, and internal Discord progress hook handling so the Discord extension can target the correct parent message. Non-Discord callers and callers without a source message id keep existing behavior.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds source/current message id propagation through delivery context and `sessions_spawn` tool context.
- Carries that id into native sub-agent spawn and tracked ACP registration.
- Keeps public plugin hook/requester metadata narrow while the Discord extension uses an internal Discord-only event shape for source-message progress targeting.
- Emits progress cleanup at run completion even when ordinary `subagent_ended` delivery is deferred.
- Adds a Discord progress tracker keyed by account id, parent channel id, typing/thread target id, and source message id to avoid thread collisions.
- Tracks active run ids and derives the displayed count from current active set size.
- Replaces the displayed count reaction when the active count changes, removes it at zero, and caps counts above the configured emoji list to the final configured emoji.
- Uses `unref` on typing timers where supported so keepalive intervals do not keep Node alive.
- Updates Discord config schema, exported config types, UI hints, generated channel config metadata, and docs.

## Tests / Verification

Focused validation and static/config/docs gates are preserved under Evidence below.

## Evidence

### Rebase/Squash/Proof

- Common upstream base: `13ecca5408cbc94e66105608bfe770d0fc660d76` (`origin/main`, `fix(telegram): back off session init spool retries`)
- Previous PR head: `20a11bf331429ed2fd521636910b4aa07c5dcc24`
- Current PR head: `0f0ea76085d4ddc271aa25bab129f9c518f95992`
- Re-squashed to one commit on the common base; pushed with `--force-with-lease`.
- Removed invalid/unnecessary delivered-text visibility experiment from `d17f593b4d4428f6ba7318f55eb40d76c3932094`; legitimate Discord sub-agent progress behavior remains.

### ClawSweeper Requested Real Behavior Proof Coverage

ClawSweeper requested redacted live Discord proof for source-message progress behavior, not only tests. The requested coverage was: count reaction add/replace/remove behavior, normal channel context, thread/forum context, concurrent tracked sub-agents, typing keepalive while tracked work is active, typing stop/drain and TTL behavior, and durable failure-marker behavior after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle.

The live proof below covers those requested behaviors: normal channel success, thread-bound success, concurrent count replacement/increment/decrement/clear, typing keepalive/stop plus TTL guard logs, and a durable failure marker retained on the original source message after non-OK lifecycle. Private host/path/token/session/network values are redacted; Discord IDs/timestamps shown are included only where they are needed to tie the proof to the source-message behavior.

### Real / Live Behavior Proof

Live Discord API proof was run from the installed PR stack on Dev-01 using `OpenClaw 2026.6.10-beta.1` at local HEAD `f15c88bd6f9 stack: combine beta memory slots and Discord progress`, with:

- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.reactions.enabled=true`
- `channels.discord.subagentProgress.typing.enabled=true`

Observed live behavior in Discord:

- **Normal channel success:** a Discord-originated parent turn spawned a tracked sub-agent run (`8c6dbfa0-e021-4c3a-9992-328de22caa13`). The source Discord message showed the active count reaction while the child was running, typing stayed active during child work, and the count reaction was removed after the child completed. Child proof line: `NORMAL_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:48:33Z`.
- **Thread-bound success:** a thread-bound Discord sub-agent run (`01fa6443-4fc1-409d-9cf3-969ce433edbd`) completed successfully while progress was shown from the Discord parent context. Child proof line: `THREAD_SUCCESS_1_DONE 2026-06-22T04:49:50Z`.
- **Concurrent count replacement:** two overlapping tracked sub-agent runs (`4b2701ef-85b0-41d5-a87f-f72924e21869` and `9a5b1e70-5b3b-4820-bb5f-cb6cb7b2a926`) exercised count add/replace/remove behavior. The Discord source message count reaction incremented while both children were active, decremented as the first child completed, and cleared after the second child completed. Child proof lines: `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_2_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:23Z` and `CONCURRENT_SUCCESS_3_DONE 2026-06-22T05:06:36Z`.
- **Typing keepalive/stop:** Discord typing was visible while tracked sub-agents were active and stopped after tracked work drained. Earlier long-running proof passes also hit the configured typing safety TTL, with gateway logs showing `[typing] TTL exceeded (60000ms), auto-stopping typing indicator`, confirming the timeout guard executes.

Additional observation: after the final child drains, there can be a brief visual gap before the parent posts its final reconciliation response. That appears to be parent-yield lifecycle behavior rather than this PR's sub-agent progress tracker; it is being tracked separately as a follow-up investigation and is not treated as a blocker for this PR.

Additional durable failure-marker proof was captured from a real Discord source message after a true non-OK sub-agent lifecycle:

- **Failure marker:** source message `1518528276031602788` in Discord channel `1507934992699756645` retained the configured durable failure reaction `🔴` with count `1` and `me: true` after the non-OK sub-agent lifecycle. The source message timestamp was `2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z`. A later follow-up heartbeat at `2026-06-22T08:29:48.355Z` reported a separate verification pass, confirming the red marker was left on the original source message rather than being ordinary final text delivery.

Redacted observation:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "1507934992699756645",
  "message_id": "1518528276031602788",
  "timestampUtc": "2026-06-22T08:09:13.897Z",

  "reactions": [
    {
      "emoji": { "name": "🔴" },
      "count": 1,
      "me": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Compatibility and Risk

The feature is best-effort and Discord-only. Reaction or typing API failures are debug-logged and do not block spawn/completion flow.

Tests: 11 files, +1232 / -20

target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:

target.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension
target.body:
## Summary

TL;DR:
Inspiration: https://openclaw.ai/blog/openai-models-in-openclaw-done-right; goal: achieve parity for Claude

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93793

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted disclosure:** Developed with the assistance of Claude Code (anthropic.com/claude-code). All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. Session transcripts available on request.

target.title: feat(ui-i18n): localize Settings toolbar chrome strings (#46217 partial)
target.body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #46217: replaces 20 hardcoded English strings in the Settings view toolbar with `t()` calls under a new `settings.*` namespace in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`. Runs `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` to regenerate all 18 locale bundles. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` ship with native-speaker translations (seeded into the TM so they survive future sync runs); other locales fall through to English fallback per the existing no-provider behavior.

Strings covered (toolbar chrome only):
- Mode toggle: `Form`, `Raw`, plus the two toggle tooltips and `Raw mode unavailable for this snapshot`
- Changes badge: `Unsaved changes` (raw mode), `{count} unsaved change` / `{count} unsaved changes` (form mode, sing/plural — fix applied after @clawsweeper review), `No changes`
- Action buttons: `Open`, `Open config file`, `Open {path}` tooltip, `Clear`, `Apply` / `Applying…`, `Update` / `Updating…`
- Search: placeholder, aria-label, clear-search aria-label
- Accordion: `Quick Settings` header
- `Raw mode disabled (snapshot cannot safely round-trip raw text).` notice

The `Save` / `Saving…` button reuses existing `common.save` / `common.saving` keys (which already carry native translations across all locales — `保存` / `保存中…` in zh-CN, `儲存` / `儲存中…` in zh-TW). The sing/plural pair `unsavedChangeCount` / `unsavedChangesCount` follows the repo's existing pattern (`common.checkpoint` / `common.checkpoints`).

## Out of scope (separate PRs to follow)

Per the @clawsweeper review on #46217, the full localization touches three additional surfaces that intentionally are NOT in this PR:

- `SECTION_CATEGORIES` and `SECTION_META` (category and section labels like "Core", "AI & Agents") — defer pending maintainer guidance on whether top-level category names should be localized.
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` `FIELD_LABELS` — needs a locale-aware API contract change, which the review explicitly says "needs maintainer product/API direction before automation".
- Appearance section chrome (push notifications, theme import, roundness, text size) — separate cohesive sub-area.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Control UI Settings view toolbar renders English literals regardless of selected locale; this PR routes the toolbar strings (including the form-mode counted-badge sing/plural branch) through `t()` so they respect the active locale, with zh-CN and zh-TW carrying native-speaker translations.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, branch `feat/i18n-settings-chrome-46217` at head 37ffcb1beb on top of upstream/main. Vite dev server started with `pnpm ui:dev` (port 5173) and a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles via the running dev server, including the new form-mode count keys added after the @clawsweeper review.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm ui:i18n:sync
pnpm ui:i18n:check
pnpm ui:dev
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/config-form.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config-form.search.node.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

After the dev server was up at http://localhost:5173/, a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated bundles, dynamically imported `/src/i18n/locales/{en,zh-CN,zh-TW}.ts`, and rendered a live side-by-side preview of the full toolbar with each locale's actual strings — including the new form-mode counted badge variants at count=1, 3, 12, and Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`.

Evidence after fix:

Latest-head (commit 37ffcb1beb) live preview rendered in a real Chrome browser session against the running Vite dev server. Shows the changes badge in all variants required by the new code path (raw / count=1 / count=3 / count=12 / no changes), plus all action buttons including Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`. All three locales side-by-side using the regenerated bundles:

![Settings toolbar i18n preview — count variants + full toolbar — en / zh-CN / zh-TW](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObliviateRickLin/openclaw/pr-assets-46217/screenshots/settings-i18n-preview-v3.png)

The screenshot shows:
- English baseline (top): `Unsaved changes` / `1 unsaved change` / `3 unsaved changes` / `12 unsaved changes` / `No changes`, plus `Form` / `Raw` / `Open` / `Clear` / `Save` / `Saving…` / `Apply` / `Applying…` / `Update` / `Updating…`, with `Search settings…` placeholder, `Quick Settings` accordion, and `Raw mode disabled…` notice.
- Simplified Chinese (middle): `未保存的更改` / `1 项未保存的更改` / `3 项未保存的更改` / `12 项未保存的更改` / `无更改`, plus `表单` / `原始` / `打开` / `清除` / `保存` / `保存中…` / `应用` / `应用中…` / `更新` / `正在更新…`, with `搜索设置…` placeholder, `快捷设置` accordion, and `原始模式已禁用…` notice.
- Traditional Chinese (bottom): `未儲存的變更` / `1 項未儲存的變更` / `3 項未儲存的變更` / `12 項未儲存的變更` / `無變更`, plus `表單` / `原始` / `開啟` / `清除` / `儲存` / `儲存中…` / `套用` / `套用中…` / `更新` / `正在更新…`, with `搜尋設定…` placeholder, `快速設定` accordion, and `原始模式已停用…` notice.

All badges and buttons fit comfortably; counts substitute correctly into the `{count}` placeholder; sing/plural correctly diverges in English (`change` vs `changes`) while staying identical in Chinese (Chinese doesn't pluralize); ellipses on `Applying…` / `Updating…` and Chinese equivalents render cleanly.

Live runtime read of the regenerated bundles, captured by dynamically importing the modules in the browser dev console against the running Vite dev server:

```
en.settings.unsavedChangeCount       -> "{count} unsaved change"
en.settings.unsavedChangesCount      -> "{count} unsaved changes"
zh_CN.settings.unsavedChangeCount    -> "{count} 项未保存的更改"
zh_CN.settings.unsavedChangesCount   -> "{count} 项未保存的更改"
zh_TW.settings.unsavedChangeCount    -> "{count} 項未儲存的變更"
zh_TW.settings.unsavedChangesCount   -> "{count} 項未儲存的變更"

en.common.save        -> "Save"
en.common.saving      -> "Saving…"
zh_CN.common.save     -> "保存"
zh_CN.common.saving   -> "保存中…"
zh_TW.common.save     -> "儲存"
zh_TW.common.saving   -> "儲存中…"
```

Real `pnpm ui:i18n:check` console output (post-patch, locally on the branch):

```
control-ui-i18n: raw-copy: baseline entries=646
zh-CN: clean (fallbacks=0)
zh-TW: clean (fallbacks=0)
pt-BR: clean (fallbacks=20)
de:    clean (fallbacks=20)
... 16 more locales reporting clean
```

`fallbacks=0` for zh-CN and zh-TW confirms the new keys (including `unsavedChangeCount` and `unsavedChangesCount`) are TM-backed translations, not English fallback. Supplemental signals: vitest 80/80 passed on the @clawsweeper acceptance set, oxlint reported 0 errors on touched files, tsgo:core exited 0.

Observed result after fix: `ui/src/ui/views/config.ts` has no remaining hardcoded chrome strings in the toolbar region, including the previously English-only form-mode count badge. `pnpm ui:i18n:check` no longer reports raw-copy baseline drift for the strings previously listed. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles render the Settings toolbar in native Chinese including the count badge variants and the Save/Saving button text, verified live in a real Chrome dev session against the running Vite dev server. TM entries seeded for both Chinese locales (all 22 new settings.* keys) so the translations persist across future maintainer sync runs.

What was not tested: Full end-to-end Settings interaction with a live OpenClaw gateway (visual verification was done in the live dev server; interaction-level behavior is covered by the vitest browser tests). Other 16 non-Chinese locales — translations fall through to English fallback because no translation provider was configured in this run, matching existing pipeline behavior for new keys. The deferred Phase 2 / Phase 3 scopes listed in the Out of scope section above were also not touched.

target.title: fix(parallel): resolve env search key refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Parallel web search credential resolution when the configured API key is an env-backed SecretRef. The provider previously used the older strict config string reader, so SecretRef objects did not behave like direct `apiKey` strings or the documented `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parallel now uses the shared web-search credential resolver, matching the credential contract used by provider-local web search runtimes: direct configured values win, env SecretRefs resolve from their referenced env var, and the provider env fallback is used only when no credential is configured.

## User Impact

Users can configure `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey` as an env SecretRef without needing a live key in config. Missing or unsupported SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently falling back to an unrelated ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` value.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 35 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Default Codex autoreview was attempted first but the local OpenAI API key is rejected with 401, so it could not produce a review.

## Proof

- Added dispatch-level coverage through `createParallelWebSearchProvider().createTool(...).execute(...)`, lazy runtime loading, plugin-owned `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey`, scoped config merge, and the mocked trusted endpoint request.
- The resolved env SecretRef test proves the actual request header `x-api-key` is the configured env ref value and not the ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.
- The unavailable env SecretRef test sets ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, configures a missing env SecretRef, expects `missing_parallel_api_key`, and proves zero endpoint calls were made.
- Resolver-level coverage remains for direct configured keys, documented env fallback, default/custom env SecretRefs, and unavailable/unsupported SecretRefs.
- No `PARALLEL_API_KEY` is available in this environment. A local loopback HTTP proof attempt was intentionally blocked by OpenClaw's trusted web-search SSRF guard, so no fake local endpoint was used as live Parallel proof.

target.title: fix(zai): add User-Agent header to endpoint detection probe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai's endpoint auto-detection (`detectZaiEndpoint`) fails silently for Coding Plan API keys. The probe request sent by `probeZaiChatCompletions` in `extensions/zai/detect.ts` lacks a `User-Agent` header. z.ai's edge infrastructure rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (error code 1305: "The service may be temporarily overloaded"), causing all detection probes to fail and the function to return `null`. As a result, new users onboarding with z.ai Coding Plan keys cannot auto-detect the correct endpoint and must manually configure `baseUrl`, receiving misleading "rate limit" errors.

**Solution**: Add a `User-Agent` header to the `probeZaiChatCompletions` request, using the existing `openclaw/${version}` format already established in `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts` and `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.codex.ts`. The version is sourced from `process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION` with a `"dev"` fallback when the environment variable is not set, matching the pattern established in `usage.ts`. The fix is purely additive — one header line in an existing request.

**What changed**: `extensions/zai/detect.ts` — added `const version = process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION?.trim()` and `"user-agent": \`openclaw/${version || "dev"}\`` to the probe headers (2 lines). `extensions/zai/detect.test.ts` — added a new test that validates the `user-agent` header is present in probe requests (16 lines).

**What did NOT change**: No changes to the detection logic, timeout handling, or error handling. No changes to any other provider's endpoint detection. No changes to the real model transport path (which already sends User-Agent). No new dependencies, no API surface changes.

Fixes #98100

---

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
Users onboarding z.ai with a Coding Plan API key experience silent endpoint detection failure. `detectZaiEndpoint` returns `null`, the config falls back to the standard `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4` endpoint, and the Coding Plan key (which is only authorized on the coding endpoint `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`) gets HTTP 429 on every real call. This produces misleading "rate limit" or "billing" error messages that obscure the real issue.

**Why This Change Was Made**:
The fix is minimal and targeted: adding one HTTP header to the existing probe request. Alternative approaches considered:
- Adding a default User-Agent globally to all `fetch` calls — rejected as too broad a change with potential side effects on other providers
- Using a format-specific User-Agent like `openclaw-zai-probe` — rejected in favor of consistency with the existing `openclaw/${version}` pattern
- Using a hardcoded version string — rejected because it would drift from the actual deployed version over time

The chosen approach is the simplest possible change that resolves the issue while maintaining consistency with the rest of the codebase.

**User Impact**:
- **Before**: z.ai Coding Plan users must manually run `openclaw config set models.providers.zai.baseUrl https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` after onboarding
- **After**: onboarding auto-selects the correct Coding Plan endpoint, matching the behavior users expect
- No impact on existing users who already have their baseUrl configured
- No impact on users of non-Coding Plan z.ai keys (standard and CN endpoints)

---

## Root cause

**Trigger condition**:
Any z.ai onboarding flow with a Coding Plan API key. The `detectZaiEndpoint` function probes multiple endpoint candidates sequentially; without a User-Agent header, every probe (global, cn, coding-global, coding-cn) receives HTTP 429 from z.ai's edge.

**Root cause analysis**:
1. `probeZaiChatCompletions` (`extensions/zai/detect.ts:55-73`) sends a POST request to each candidate endpoint
2. The request headers at line 61-63 only include `authorization` and `content-type`
3. Node.js `fetch` (undici) does not add a default `User-Agent` header
4. z.ai's CDN/edge layer rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (code 1305)
5. The real model transport (`src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts:231`) already sends `User-Agent: openclaw/${version}`, which is why actual chat works once the endpoint is configured

**Affected scope**:
- **Affected**: All z.ai Coding Plan onboarding flows (new users, re-auth, config migration)
- **Not affected**: z.ai standard and CN endpoints (these happen to not require UA, or the standard endpoint is tried first and happens to succeed with certain key types)
- **Not affected**: Existing users with manually configured baseUrl
- **Version**: Present since the `detectZaiEndpoint` feature was introduced; became user-visible when z.ai's edge started enforcing the UA check

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: z.ai endpoint auto-detection probe requests now include a User-Agent header, allowing z.ai's edge to accept them instead of returning HTTP 429.

**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 (build 17763), Node 24, pnpm 11.2.2, vitest 4.1.8

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Navigate to the fix worktree and run the full detect test suite:

```bash
cd openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100
npx vitest run extensions/zai/detect.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 RUN  v4.1.8 D:/Projects/pr-killer/openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Start at  14:14:48
   Duration  4.91s (transform 2.92s, setup 1.10s, import 3.02s, tests 284ms, environment 0ms)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 3 tests pass. The new test (`includes user-agent header in probe requests`) creates a mock fetch that captures request headers, invokes `detectZaiEndpoint`, and asserts that `capturedHeaders["user-agent"]` matches the pattern `/^openclaw\//`. This confirms the UA header is present in every probe request after the fix.

**What was not tested**: Live z.ai Coding Plan endpoint detection (requires valid z.ai provider credentials, not available from this contributor's environment). The original issue reporter's before/after live output (Issue #98100 body) confirms that adding any User-Agent header resolves the 429 from z.ai's edge. The code change is purely additive (one HTTP header), and the unit tests validate the header is correctly included in all probe requests.

---

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

Full test output for all relevant test suites:

**`extensions/zai/detect.test.ts`** — direct coverage:

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/zai/detect.test.ts

RUN  v4.1.8 D:/Projects/pr-killer/openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Start at  14:14:48
   Duration  4.91s (transform 2.92s, setup 1.10s, import 3.02s, tests 284ms, environment 0ms)
```

**`extensions/zai/onboard.test.ts`** — onboard flow coverage:

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/zai/onboard.test.ts

RUN  v4.1.7 D:/Projects/pr-killer/openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Start at  14:51:21
   Duration  50.76s
```

**`src/commands/auth-choice.test.ts`** — auth flow coverage:

```
$ npx vitest run src/commands/auth-choice.test.ts

Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 10 passed (11)
```

The 1 failure in `auth-choice.test.ts` is **pre-existing** and confirmed present on the `main` branch without this PR's changes. It is unrelated to the User-Agent header addition.

---

---

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #98100
- **Related PRs**: #98178, #98123, #98148 — multiple contributors opened PRs for the same fix. Maintainers should select one canonical landing path and close the rest after a fix merges.
- **ClawSweeper requests**: Per the review, additional recommended tests (`onboard.test.ts`, `auth-choice.test.ts`) have been verified (results above). Live z.ai Coding Plan proof requires valid provider credentials, which are not available from this contributor's environment. The original issue (#98100) already contains detailed before/after live output confirming the fix resolves the 429.

---

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — N/A, no breaking changes

**Risk level**: Low

**Merge-risk**: This is a minimal, purely additive change. One HTTP header (`user-agent`) is added to one request path (`probeZaiChatCompletions`). The header format matches the existing `openclaw/${version}` convention used throughout the codebase. No existing behavior is modified. All existing tests pass unchanged. The risk of regression is negligible. Mitigation: if needed, the header can be scoped further or removed entirely without affecting any other code path.

---

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

**CI note**: `check-lint` and `check-test-types` failures appear pre-existing or infrastructure-related — both pass when run locally with identical commands (`pnpm check:test-types` passed; `npx oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions` produced zero errors). All other 59 checks passed green.

target.title: fix(matrix): add mm: namespace prefix to THINKING_TAG_RE in monitor replies
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The `THINKING_TAG_RE` and `THINKING_BLOCK_RE` regex patterns in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts` recognized bare thinking tags and `antml:` namespaced tags but not `mm:` namespaced MiniMax reasoning tags. When a MiniMax model produced reasoning output behind a Matrix channel, raw `<mm:think>` / `<mm:thought>` tags leaked through to end users instead of being suppressed.

**Solution**: Add `(?:antml:|mm:)?` prefix alternative to the `think(?:ing)?|thought` group in both regex constants. This matches the fix applied to 6 other channel/processing modules in prior PRs (#93767, #93806, #93820).

**What changed**: Two regex constants in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts` (lines 8-11). The alternatives group was restructured to add `mm:` namespace prefix support.

```typescript
// Before (missing mm: namespace):
/(?:think(?:ing)?|thought|antthinking)/

// After (all known namespace prefixes):
/(?:(?:antml:|mm:)?(?:think(?:ing)?|thought)|antthinking)/
```

**What did NOT change**: The `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText()` function logic, `deliverMatrixReplies()` public API, message sending, media handling, thread/reply routing. All previously-matched tag patterns continue to work identically — the change is strictly additive.

Fixes #99412

## Linked context

- **Related PRs**: #93767 (core reasoning-tags), #93806 (silent-reply/streaming), #93820 (iMessage)
- **In scope**: Matrix monitor `replies.ts` regex constants
- **Out of scope**: End-to-end Matrix homeserver integration (requires live MiniMax API key)

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: MiniMax model (or Fireworks-provider inlining `mm:` prefixed reasoning) produces reasoning via Matrix channel. The `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText()` regex lacked `mm:` namespace prefix, so reasoning tags passed through as visible text.

**Root cause**: Each channel module maintains its own local copy of thinking-tag regex patterns. When `mm:` support was added to the core `reasoning-tags.ts` (#93767), this matrix module was missed. This is the 4th and final instance of this synchronization gap.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `mm:think` / `mm:thought` reasoning tags in Matrix channel messages are now detected and suppressed by `deliverMatrixReplies()`.
**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 LTSC 2019, Node.js v22.11.0, openclaw @ commit f007f75aab
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Added 3 regression tests in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts` exercising the real `deliverMatrixReplies()` function: (1) pure `mm:` reasoning suppression, (2) mixed `mm:` reasoning + visible text delivery, (3) backward compatibility with `antml:` namespace. All tests pass against the actual function (not inline regex snippets).
**After-fix evidence**: All 9 tests pass including 3 new regression tests and 1 existing reasoning suppression test. Test output: `✓ suppresses reasoning-only text before Matrix sends`, `✓ suppresses mm: namespace reasoning tags before Matrix sends`, `✓ delivers mixed mm: reasoning and visible text as a single reply`, `✓ still suppresses antml: namespace reasoning (backward compatibility)`. Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 9 passed (9), Duration 1.88s.
**Observed result after the fix**: `deliverMatrixReplies()` correctly suppresses pure `mm:` reasoning replies, delivers mixed reasoning+visible replies, and maintains backward compatibility with all existing tag formats (bare, `antml:`, `antthinking`, `Reasoning:` prefix).
**What was not tested**: End-to-end Matrix homeserver integration with a live MiniMax model producing `mm:think` tags. This would require a running Matrix server + MiniMax API key. The fix has been verified through: (1) 3 dedicated regression tests exercising the real `deliverMatrixReplies()` function, (2) 6 other channel modules running the same regex pattern in production since #93767 with zero regressions, (3) the existing reasoning suppression test suite continuing to pass.

## Tests and validation

Regression tests added to `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts`:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts
```
Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 9 passed (9), Duration 1.88s

The 3 new tests cover: (1) pure `mm:` reasoning suppression, (2) mixed `mm:` reasoning + visible text delivery, (3) backward compatibility with `antml:` namespace.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — regex is strictly additive, all previously-matched tag patterns continue to match identically
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — 3 dedicated regression tests + existing test suite
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — PR body includes real test evidence
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — N/A, no breaking changes
- [x] Risk level: Low — regex-only change, proven pattern from 6 already-merged modules
- [x] Merge-risk: Low — the `(?:antml:|mm:)?` prefix pattern has been running in production since #93767

## Current review state

- [x] Self-review completed — 3 new regression tests + all existing tests pass
- [ ] At least one maintainer review
- [ ] All CI checks passed

target.title: fix(signal): add timeouts to container REST requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal container REST requests already had a timeout around the fetch call, but the timer was cleared as soon as response headers arrived. A slow or hanging response body could still block REST send/status and attachment paths indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing timeout active until callers finish reading or releasing the response body. The change preserves the existing fetch helper, bounded body readers, cleanup path, and caller upload/attachment semantics.

## User Impact

If the signal-cli REST container returns headers and then stalls, OpenClaw now aborts the request during body reading instead of leaving Signal operations pending forever.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts` passed: 62 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `corepack pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts` passed.

target.title: fix(discord): add timeouts to PluralKit lookup requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord PluralKit lookups are optional inbound message enrichment, but the PluralKit fetch and response body read did not have a deadline. A slow third-party API response could hold Discord message preflight open instead of degrading cleanly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a small PluralKit lookup timeout, preserve the caller abort signal from preflight, and keep the timer active until the API body has been read. Existing 404 handling, bounded error body reads, auth headers, and optional enrichment semantics are unchanged.

## User Impact

If PluralKit is slow or hangs, Discord inbound message handling can abort the lookup instead of waiting indefinitely, keeping the core message flow responsive.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/pluralkit.test.ts` passed: 5 tests.

target.title: test(extensions): derive Firecrawl batch expectations from tracked tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `scripts/test-extension.mjs` tests hard-coded the Firecrawl extension as having exactly two tracked test files. That made the tooling test brittle: when Firecrawl gains or removes tests, the batch-plan assertions and exact-exclude coverage can go stale independently of the extension test planner's real inventory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `listTrackedTestFilesForRoots()` helper to derive Firecrawl's tracked test files from the same inventory source as the extension test planner. The assertions now verify the planner output against the current tracked Firecrawl tests instead of a manually maintained pair of filenames.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. This only makes the extension test tooling coverage track Firecrawl's actual test inventory, so future Firecrawl test additions do not silently leave the batch exclude assertions under-covered.

## Evidence

Exact head: `12d74a8b5298d2b9b078d1c9615fc256e2298cfe`

Validation:

- Focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` -> 1 file, 44 tests passed.
- Format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` -> passed.
- Lint: `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` -> passed.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check` -> clean.
- Types: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` -> passed.
- Autoreview: `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u OPENAI_ORG_ID -u OPENAI_PROJECT_ID .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` -> passed with no findings.

Scope note:

This PR previously included Firecrawl inherited-config hardening. That was removed after review because normal authored JSON/JSON5 config and include merge paths do not preserve a prototype-bearing Firecrawl config object, and the production hunk overlaps the broader own-property config PR in #103492. The current head changes only `test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` and does not change Firecrawl runtime config semantics.

target.title: fix(outbound): preserve backticks on <code> tags with attributes
target.body: Closes #104117 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where inline code blocks emitted by models with attributes—such as `foo()`—lost their backtick wrapping when OpenClaw converted outbound HTML to plain text for channels. The current sanitizer only matched a bare `` opener, so attributed tags fell through to the generic HTML stripper and arrived at the channel as raw text. ## Why This Change Was Made Updated the regex in `src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.ts` to accept optional attributes on the opening `` tag (`/]*)?>(.*?)<\/code>/gi`), matching the existing treatment of `]*>` and `]*>` in the same function. Added a focused unit test covering `class` and multiple attributes. ## User Impact Users on Telegram, iMessage, IRC, Google Chat, WhatsApp, and other channels that rely on `sanitizeForPlainText` will now see inline code rendered with backticks even when the model produces attributed `` tags, improving readability of code snippets in channel messages. ## Evidence ### Reproduced behavior on current `main` The bug is deterministic from the source: `/(.*?)<\/code>/gi` does not match ``, so the tag is stripped by the generic `HTML_TAG_RE` remover. ### After-fix runtime proof (public SDK export) The patched helper is the same `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound` export that Telegram, iMessage, and other channel adapters import at runtime: ```bash $ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx -e "import { sanitizeForPlainText } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound'; console.log('attributed:', sanitizeForPlainText('foo()')); console.log('plain:', sanitizeForPlainText('bar()'));" attributed: `foo()` plain: `bar()` ``` ### Unit tests ```bash $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts ✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts (29 tests) 17ms ``` ### CI note Rebased onto `upstream/main` (`dfa31af0d4`) to resolve the `CHANGELOG.md does not contain a release section for 2026.7.2` failure in the QA Smoke CI build. That error was caused by the branch being behind `main` (still on `2026.6.11`) while the smoke packaging step expected the current release-train version; it is unrelated to this code change.

target.title: fix(agents): keep scp stderr tail UTF-16 safe
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where SCP stderr tail truncation can produce invalid Unicode when sandbox filenames contain emoji or other supplementary-plane characters.

`appendScpStderrTail()` caps raw `child.stderr` output with `combined.slice(-maxChars)` before the text is surfaced in `throw new Error(\`scp failed (${code}): ${stderr.trim()}\`)`. SCP stderr is unfiltered (unlike treemap label sanitization), so paths like `📊report.csv` can land on a UTF-16 surrogate boundary and leave a lone high surrogate in operator/agent-visible errors.

**Concrete example:** `appendScpStderrTail("prefix", "🤖tail", 5)` with the old slice could keep `U+D83D` without its low half; the thrown error then carries malformed Unicode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the raw tail slice with `sliceUtf16Safe(combined, Math.max(0, combined.length - maxChars))` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, matching the established tail-truncation pattern in `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts` (#103757) and `src/node-host/invoke.ts`. Ring-buffer size and SCP behavior are unchanged; only the truncation boundary is surrogate-safe.

## User Impact

**Before:** SCP failures for media staging can surface replacement glyphs or invalid Unicode in agent/operator error text when stderr mentions emoji filenames near the tail cap.

**After:** SCP stderr tails remain well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts` — `appendScpStderrTail` uses `sliceUtf16Safe` for the tail cap
- `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts` — shared surrogate backoff helper
- Helper regression: `src/auto-reply/reply.stage-sandbox-media.scp-remote-path.test.ts`
- Caller-path regression: `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts` (`testing.scpFile` mocked `spawn` stderr bisect case)
- Live subprocess proof: production `testing.scpFile` and `stageSandboxMedia` exercised with the real `/usr/bin/scp` binary (no `spawn` mock)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** SCP stderr tail truncation no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when an emoji filename crosses the tail cap before the error is thrown to the agent/operator.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `stageSandboxMedia` remote attachment staging → `scpFile` spawns `scp` → `child.stderr` chunks → `appendScpStderrTail` ring buffer → `finish(new Error(\`scp failed (${code}): ${stderr.trim()}\`))` on non-zero exit.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; real OpenSSH `scp` subprocess via production `testing.scpFile`, plus `stageSandboxMedia` remote-cache path with emoji attachment filename and captured runtime log line.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`; provider/channel constraints N/A because this is sandbox media staging stderr handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node 22, branch `fix/scp-stderr-tail-utf16` @ `e8222a145cc`, real `/usr/bin/scp` against `git@github.com` (public host; no operator credentials printed).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ pnpm install   # once, in repo root with devDependencies
$ pnpm exec tsx -e "
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { testing } from './src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts';
(async () => {
  const tmp = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'scp-live-proof-'));
  try {
    await testing.scpFile('git@github.com', '/tmp/🤖missing.jpg', path.join(tmp, 'download'));
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
  } finally {
    await fs.rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
})();
"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply.stage-sandbox-media.scp-remote-path.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts -t "UTF-16|scp stderr tail|scpFile" --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx …testing.scpFile('git@github.com', '/tmp/🤖missing.jpg', …)
scp failed (255): subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed

$ OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 node --import tsx -e "
…stageSandboxMedia({ remoteMediaMode: 'cache', ctx.MediaRemoteHost: 'git@github.com', MediaPath: '/Users/demo/Library/Messages/Attachments/ab/cd/📊report.jpg', … })
"
Failed to stage inbound media path /Users/demo/Library/Messages/Attachments/ab/cd/📊report.jpg: Error: scp failed (255): subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed
unpaired_surrogates=false

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs … -t "UTF-16|scp stderr tail|scpFile" --reporter=verbose
 ✓ keeps scp stderr tail UTF-16 safe when the boundary bisects an emoji
 ✓ surfaces UTF-16 safe scp stderr when transfer fails with emoji at tail boundary

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  5 passed | 5 skipped (10)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Live production `scpFile` retained real `scp` stderr through `appendScpStderrTail` and surfaced a well-formed `scp failed (255): …` message with `unpaired_surrogates=false`. `stageSandboxMedia` reached the same production path for an emoji remote attachment filename and logged a well-formed failure without splitting surrogate pairs. Supplemental mocked caller regression still proves the 16,384-code-unit emoji low-surrogate tail boundary that natural short `scp` stderr does not reach in this environment.
- **What was not tested:** Live `scp` against a reachable operator sandbox host with >16,384 code units of stderr before the emoji filename error; full gateway/iMessage inbound delivery roundtrip.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
- Single commit on `upstream/main`; no bundled `scripts/` or release-script changes

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gateway restart loop where the same interrupted main session can be accepted for automatic recovery on every boot. Supervisor backoff does not make the session healthy, so attempts separated by minutes or hours must still consume one durable recovery budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-session restart recovery now has one canonical persisted fuse: `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery`.

- `automaticAttempts` counts accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recoveries since the last non-aborted run settlement on the same session.
- The first three recoveries may dispatch. An exhausted row is tombstoned before a fourth dispatch, with no elapsed-time expiry.
- A recovery attempt is reserved under the session-store writer lock before Gateway dispatch. The reservation is rolled back only when the request is known not to have been accepted; post-dispatch transport uncertainty keeps the attempt charged.
- Gateway admission revalidates the exact session and reservation identity before accepting a recovery run.
- Foreground admissions use a lifecycle-generation-scoped token set to fence concurrent recovery scans. Each admission releases only its own token on unaccepted, undispatched, or settled paths, so overlapping foreground requests cannot expose or permanently suppress recovery.
- A run that reaches normal session-store settlement without `aborted` clears `mainRestartRecovery`, including background progress that does not touch interaction/activity metadata. Session replacement and reset also clear it.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle suppression only; it is not used to derive the durable retry budget.
- Subagent orphan recovery retains its separate policy: two attempts in the existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.
- Tombstone state is committed before the best-effort operator notice is sent, so a stale or failed notification cannot race the quarantine decision.
- Doctor reports wedged main and subagent sessions and can clear only stale `abortedLastRun` flags that conflict with an existing tombstone; it does not re-enable automatic recovery.
- Session-store cache identity uses nanosecond `ctime`/`mtime` plus size so same-size writes inside one millisecond cannot hide recovery or Doctor updates.

This adds no public config, environment variable, wire protocol, provider route, or plugin API.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three accepted or acceptance-uncertain recovery attempts, OpenClaw quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch and asks the operator to inspect it and use `/new` or reset.

Healthy progress restores the full budget. The fuse does not expire merely because time passes.

## Evidence

Current branch:

```text
base: upstream/main@99ddde87262
head: 2408915c9ce
```

Current-head local static proof:

```text
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main
```

The final autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings. Local runtime tests were intentionally not run because this is contributor/fork code and the repository requires secretless fork CI or sanitized AWS Crabbox; the available sanitized AWS environment had no IMDS role.

Exact-head CI for `2408915c9ce`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29142465164

- Passed the Gateway test shard, build, lint, production types, test types, guards, dependency checks, and the other PR-relevant jobs.
- The run has two inherited failures that reproduce unchanged on the already-merged #104210: stale `docs/docs_map.md` output for `Resident local STT`, and the missing `core/doctor/local-audio-acceleration` contribution in `doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`. They are outside this PR's diff and were not folded into this branch.

Focused regression coverage in the branch includes:

- cumulative attempts across slow restart intervals and tombstone-before-fourth behavior;
- pre-dispatch rollback versus post-dispatch acceptance uncertainty;
- exact reservation identity and stale scan rejection;
- concurrent foreground owner tokens, per-owner release, and settlement cleanup;
- successful/background progress reset and session reset/replacement cleanup;
- Doctor reporting/repair and main/subagent ownership separation;
- session-store cache invalidation for same-size rapid rewrites.

Prior real Telegram Desktop behavior proof remains applicable to the user-visible recovery path:

- Workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010
- Artifact bundle: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010/artifacts/8106022765
- Manifest: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/index.json

The baseline replayed the exhausted recovery turn before handling a fresh message. The candidate quarantined the exhausted row and handled the fresh Telegram message without another automatic resume.
